properties.key: A stable name for the control. Lists use it to keep each item's state when items move, and it stays the same across updates.
properties.data: Any value you attach to the control, such as an id; read it back in handlers with `event.control.props["data"]`.
properties.label: Text label shown for the control.
properties.content: The single child control rendered inside this control.
properties.title: The control shown as the title.
properties.subtitle: The control shown as the secondary line below the title.
properties.leading: Control placed before the main content (e.g. an icon or avatar).
properties.trailing: Control placed after the main content.
properties.actions: Controls shown in the trailing action area.
properties.icon: Icon name shown by the control.
properties.src: Source URL or asset path of the image.
properties.url: URL the control loads or links to.
properties.options: The selectable options (built with the control's option helper).
properties.disabled: Disables the control and every control inside it: they stop reacting to input and stop sending events.
properties.visible: Hides the control when false; a hidden control takes no space.
properties.divisions: Number of discrete steps between min and max.
properties.hint_text: Placeholder shown when the field is empty.
properties.helper_text: Helper text shown below the field.
properties.error_text: Error message shown below the field; also marks it invalid.
properties.password: Obscures the entered text when true.
properties.multiline: Allows multiple lines of input when true.
properties.read_only: Prevents editing while still allowing selection.
properties.clip_behavior: How content overflowing the bounds is clipped.
properties.expand: Inside a `row`, a `column` or the page, fills the free space along the parent's main axis. `true` is a share of 1; an integer sets the share, so `expand: 2` gets twice the space of `expand: 1`. Other parents ignore it.
properties.expand_loose: With `expand`, lets the control stay smaller than its share instead of filling it.
properties.padding: Inner spacing between the border and the content.
properties.margin: Space around the control, in logical pixels: one number for every side, or `{ left:, top:, right:, bottom: }`.
properties.align: Aligns the control in the space its parent gives it, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1 (`{ x: 0, y: 0 }` is the center).
properties.alignment: Alignment of the content within the control.
properties.aspect_ratio: Keeps the control at this width-to-height ratio, for example `16 / 9.0`.
properties.col: Columns the control spans in its parent `responsive_row`: a number, or a hash per breakpoint such as `{ "xs" => 12, "md" => 6 }` (default: all of them). Other parents ignore it.
properties.top: Distance from the top edge of the parent `stack`, in logical pixels. Only a child of a `stack` can be positioned; elsewhere the control shows an error.
properties.bottom: Distance from the bottom edge of the parent `stack`, in logical pixels. Only a child of a `stack` can be positioned; elsewhere the control shows an error.
properties.left: Distance from the left edge of the parent `stack`, in logical pixels. Only a child of a `stack` can be positioned; elsewhere the control shows an error.
properties.right: Distance from the right edge of the parent `stack`, in logical pixels. Only a child of a `stack` can be positioned; elsewhere the control shows an error.
properties.rotate: Rotates the control clockwise by an angle in radians, such as `Math::PI / 4`, or by `{ angle:, alignment: }` to turn it around another point. Its parent still lays it out unrotated.
properties.scale: Scales the control: `1` is its normal size and `0.5` half of it. `{ scale_x:, scale_y: }` scales each axis on its own.
properties.offset: Moves the control by a fraction of its own size, as `{ x:, y: }`: `{ x: 1, y: 0 }` shifts it one width to the right. Its parent still lays it out at the original place.
properties.rtl: Lays the control out right to left when true.
properties.adaptive: Accepted for Flet compatibility; no Ruflet client reads it. The design always follows the platform: Cupertino widgets on iOS and macOS, Material widgets everywhere else.
properties.tooltip: Text shown when the user hovers over the control or long-presses it.
properties.badge: A badge on the control's corner: a String label such as `"3"`, or `badge(...)` for a styled one.
properties.mouse_cursor: Cursor shown when hovering the control.
properties.animate_opacity: Animates changes to `opacity`: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `animation(300, curve: "easeOut")`.
properties.animate_size: Animates changes to `width` and `height`, or to the content's own size when neither is set: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `animation(300, curve: "easeOut")`.
properties.animate_scale: Animates changes to `scale`: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `animation(300, curve: "easeOut")`.
properties.animate_rotation: Animates changes to `rotate`: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `animation(300, curve: "easeOut")`.
properties.animate_offset: Animates changes to `offset`: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `animation(300, curve: "easeOut")`.
properties.animate_position: Animates changes to `left`, `top`, `right` and `bottom` inside a `stack`: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `animation(300, curve: "easeOut")`.
properties.animate_margin: Animates changes to `margin`: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `animation(300, curve: "easeOut")`.
properties.animate_align: Animates changes to `align`: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `animation(300, curve: "easeOut")`.
properties.size_change_interval: Minimum time between two `on_size_change` events, in milliseconds (default 10).
properties.action: A client action, built with `Ruflet.client_action`, that the client runs inside the tap before it sends `on_click`. Use it for work browsers allow only during a user gesture, such as opening a link, copying to the clipboard or picking files.
properties.spacing: Space between the control's children, or between its parts such as a checkbox and its label, in logical pixels.
properties.run_spacing: Space between lines of children when they wrap, in logical pixels.
properties.tight: Takes only as much space along the main axis as the children need.
properties.reverse: Reverses the direction: lists start from the end, and animations play backwards.
properties.horizontal: Lays the items out and scrolls them horizontally instead of vertically.
properties.scroll: Makes the content scrollable when it overflows: `"auto"`, `"adaptive"`, `"always"` or `"hidden"` (no scrollbar).
properties.scroll_interval: Minimum time between `on_scroll` events, in milliseconds (default 10).
properties.auto_scroll: Scrolls to the end automatically whenever the children change, as in a chat or log view.
properties.auto_scroll_animation: How `auto_scroll` moves to the end: a duration in milliseconds, `{ duration:, curve: }`, or `false` to jump.
properties.keyboard_dismiss_behavior: Whether scrolling closes the on-screen keyboard: `"manual"` (default) or `"onDrag"`.
properties.end_reached_threshold: How close to the end, in logical pixels, the user must scroll before `on_end_reached` fires (default 200).
properties.item_extent: Size of each item along the scroll direction, in logical pixels, such as the row height of a picker wheel.
properties.cache_extent: How far beyond the visible area, in logical pixels, the list builds items ahead of time.
properties.build_controls_on_demand: Builds only the children that are scrolled into view (default `true`).
properties.semantic_child_count: Number of items screen readers announce for the list.
properties.divider_thickness: Thickness of the dividers drawn between items or rows, in logical pixels.
properties.first_item_prototype: Uses the first item to measure the size of every item, which speeds up layout.
properties.prototype_item: A sample item used to measure the size of every item.
properties.show_default_drag_handles: Shows the platform drag handle on each item; set `false` to drag only by your own `reorderable_drag_handle`.
properties.auto_scroller_velocity_scalar: How fast the list scrolls while an item is dragged near its edge.
properties.anchor: Relative position, from 0.0 to 1.0, of the zero scroll offset in the viewport.
properties.selected_index: Index of the selected item, starting at 0.
properties.size: Size of the control: a number in logical pixels for icons, text and indicators, or a size name such as `"small"` or `"large"` for buttons.
properties.min_size: Minimum width and height of the button.
properties.opacity_on_click: Opacity, from 0.0 to 1.0, the control fades to while it is pressed.
properties.icon_size: Size of the icon, in logical pixels.
properties.gradient: Gradient that fills the control instead of a solid color.
properties.blend_mode: How the control's color or shader is combined with what is behind it, for example `"multiply"` or `"srcIn"`.
properties.border_side: Border line, for example `{ color: "#d1d5db", width: 1 }`.
properties.fit: How the content is sized into the available space: a box fit such as `"contain"` or `"cover"` for images and animations, a stack fit such as `"expand"` for stacks.
properties.repeat: Repeats the content: loops an animation, or tiles an image (`"repeat"`, `"repeatX"`, `"repeatY"`).
properties.x: Horizontal position: in logical pixels on a canvas, or the data value on the x axis in a chart.
properties.y: Vertical position: in logical pixels on a canvas, or the data value on the y axis in a chart.
properties.paint: How a canvas shape is drawn (color, stroke width, fill or stroke, gradient), built with `paint(...)`.
properties.semantics_label: Text that screen readers announce for the control.
properties.semantics_value: Value that screen readers announce, such as a progress percentage.
properties.exclude_from_semantics: Hides the control from screen readers; on a gesture detector, hides its gestures.
properties.dense: Uses a more compact layout with less vertical space.
properties.direction: Layout direction of the segments: `"horizontal"` (default) or `"vertical"`.
properties.variant: Style variant of the control, for example `"elevated"`, `"filled"` or `"outlined"` for a card.
properties.label_position: Side of the control the label is placed on: `"right"` (default) or `"left"`.
properties.toggleable: Lets a second tap clear the selection.
properties.default: Marks the action as the default one; iOS shows it in bold.
properties.destructive: Marks the action as destructive; iOS shows it in red.
properties.modal: When true, tapping outside the dialog or sheet does not close it.
properties.scrollable: Lets the content scroll when it does not fit.
properties.maintain_state: Keeps the hidden children alive while the control is collapsed.
properties.extended: Shows each label beside its icon instead of under it.
properties.label_type: Which destination labels are shown: `"all"`, `"selected"` or `"none"`.
properties.group_alignment: How the groups of items are aligned.
properties.use_indicator: Draws a highlight behind the selected destination.
properties.indicator_shape: Shape of the highlight behind the selected destination.
properties.min_width: Minimum width of the control, in logical pixels.
properties.min_extended_width: Width of the rail when `extended` is true.
properties.duration: Length of the control's animation, or how long it stays visible, in milliseconds.
properties.reverse_duration: Length of the animation for the outgoing content, in milliseconds.
properties.animation_duration: Length of the control's transition animation, in milliseconds.
properties.animation_curve: Easing curve of the control's transition animation, for example `"easeInOut"`.
properties.switch_in_curve: Easing curve for the incoming content, for example `"easeOut"`.
properties.switch_out_curve: Easing curve for the outgoing content, for example `"easeIn"`.
properties.transition: Animation between the old and the new content: `"fade"` (default), `"scale"` or `"rotation"`.
properties.animating: Runs the animation while true; set `false` to pause it.
properties.animation: Animation applied when the chart data changes: a duration in milliseconds or `{ duration:, curve: }`.
properties.begin: Value the transition animation starts from.
properties.end: Value the transition animation ends at.
properties.curve: Easing curve of the animation, for example `"easeInOut"`.
properties.delay: Time to wait before the animation starts, in milliseconds.
properties.sliding: Selects the sliding iOS segmented control; set by `cupertino_sliding_segmented_button`.
properties.interval: Time between sensor readings, in milliseconds.
properties.enabled: Turns the sensor stream on or off.
properties.cancel_on_error: Stops the sensor stream after the first error.
properties.interactive: Enables touch tooltips and highlights on the chart (default `true`).
properties.min_x: Smallest value shown on the x axis.
properties.max_x: Largest value shown on the x axis.
properties.min_y: Smallest value shown on the y axis.
properties.max_y: Largest value shown on the y axis.
properties.left_axis: Axis drawn on the left of the chart, built with `chart_axis(...)`.
properties.right_axis: Axis drawn on the right of the chart, built with `chart_axis(...)`.
properties.top_axis: Axis drawn above the chart, built with `chart_axis(...)`.
properties.bottom_axis: Axis drawn below the chart, built with `chart_axis(...)`.
properties.show_tooltip: Shows the tooltip for this data point.
properties.capitalization: Automatic capitalization of typed text: `"none"`, `"words"`, `"sentences"` or `"characters"`.
properties.text_align: Horizontal alignment of the text: `"left"`, `"center"`, `"right"`, `"justify"`, `"start"` or `"end"`.
properties.text_size: Font size of the typed text.
properties.text_vertical_align: Vertical position of the text in a tall field, from -1.0 (top) to 1.0 (bottom).
properties.error: Error shown below the field, as text or a control; it also marks the field invalid.
properties.helper: Helper text or control shown below the field.
properties.counter: Text or control shown below the field on the right, often a character count.
properties.prefix: Text or control shown inside the field before the input.
properties.suffix: Text or control shown inside the field after the input.
properties.collapsed: Removes the field's decoration and padding for a minimal input.
properties.align_label_with_hint: Aligns the label with the hint text; useful for multiline fields.
properties.fit_parent_size: Makes the field fill its parent's size.
properties.hint_fade_duration: Time the hint takes to fade when the user starts typing, in milliseconds.
properties.error_max_lines: Maximum number of lines of error text.
properties.helper_max_lines: Maximum number of lines of helper text.
properties.hint_max_lines: Maximum number of lines of hint text.
properties.max_length: Maximum number of characters the user can enter; a counter shows the count.
properties.max_lines: Maximum number of lines the control shows.
properties.min_lines: Minimum number of lines the field shows.
properties.input_filter: Limits which characters can be typed, with a regular expression.
properties.autofill_hints: Hints for the platform's autofill, for example `["email"]`.
properties.can_reveal_password: Shows an eye button that reveals a `password` field's text.
properties.obscuring_character: Character shown in place of each typed character in a `password` field.
properties.shift_enter: In a multiline field, Enter submits and Shift+Enter starts a new line.
properties.can_request_focus: Whether the field can take keyboard focus.
properties.always_call_on_tap: Fires `on_click` on every tap, even when the field already has focus.
properties.enable_interactive_selection: Lets the user select text and use copy and paste.
properties.enable_ime_personalized_learning: Lets the keyboard learn from what the user types.
properties.enable_stylus_handwriting: Allows handwriting input with a stylus where the platform supports it.
properties.ignore_up_down_keys: Ignores the up and down arrow keys in the field.
properties.keyboard_brightness: Appearance of the iOS keyboard: `"light"` or `"dark"`.
properties.smart_dashes_type: Turns iOS smart dashes on or off.
properties.smart_quotes_type: Turns iOS smart quotes on or off.
properties.shadows: Drop shadows painted behind the control.
properties.text_input_action: The keyboard's action button, such as `"next"`, `"search"` or `"done"`.
properties.placeholder_text: Prompt shown while the field is empty (Cupertino look only; `hint_text` takes precedence).
properties.clear_button_visibility_mode: When the clear button shows: `"never"`, `"editing"`, `"notEditing"` or `"always"`.
properties.clear_button_semantics_label: Label screen readers announce for the clear button.
properties.locale: Locale for month and day names, for example `{ language_code: "fr" }`.
properties.first_date: Earliest date the user can pick.
properties.last_date: Latest date the user can pick.
properties.entry_mode: How the value is entered, for example `"calendar"` or `"input"` for dates and `"dial"` or `"input"` for times.
properties.minute_interval: Step between selectable minutes, for example 5.
properties.allow_multiple_selection: Lets more than one segment be selected.
properties.allow_empty_selection: Lets the user clear the selection.
properties.round: Number of decimal places shown in the value label.
properties.suggestions: The suggestions the user can pick from.
properties.suggestions_max_height: Maximum height of the suggestion list, in logical pixels.
properties.menu_position: Where the menu opens relative to the button: `"over"` or `"under"`.
properties.foreground_image_src: Image drawn over the avatar's content, usually the user's photo.
properties.background_image_src: Image drawn behind the avatar's content.
properties.background: Control shown behind the content while it is swiped from start to end (right, or down); also used for the other direction when `secondary_background` is not set.
properties.secondary_background: Control shown behind the content while it is swiped from end to start (left, or up).
properties.dismiss_direction: Which swipes dismiss the control: `"horizontal"`, `"endToStart"`, `"startToEnd"`, `"vertical"`, `"up"`, `"down"` or `"none"`.
properties.dismiss_thresholds: Fraction of the width or height the control must travel before it is dismissed, per direction.
properties.movement_duration: Time the control takes to slide away or back, in milliseconds (default 200).
properties.resize_duration: Time the space left by a dismissed control takes to close, in milliseconds (default 300).
properties.cross_axis_end_offset: Moves the control across the swipe direction, as a fraction of its size, as it is dismissed.
properties.drag_interval: Minimum time between drag update events, in milliseconds.
properties.hover_interval: Minimum time between hover events, in milliseconds.
properties.multi_tap_touches: Number of fingers that `on_multi_tap` waits for.
properties.allowed_devices: Pointer kinds that can start a gesture, for example `["touch", "mouse"]`.
properties.trackpad_scroll_causes_scale: Treats two-finger trackpad scrolling as a pinch.
properties.sort_column_index: Index of the column that shows the sort arrow.
properties.sort_ascending: Direction of the sort arrow: `true` for ascending.
properties.show_checkbox_column: Adds a checkbox column for selecting rows.
properties.show_bottom_border: Draws a border below the last row.
properties.column_spacing: Space between columns, in logical pixels.
properties.horizontal_margin: Space before the first and after the last column, in logical pixels.
properties.checkbox_horizontal_margin: Space around the row checkboxes, in logical pixels.
properties.horizontal_lines: Border line between rows, for example `{ color: "#e5e7eb", width: 1 }`.
properties.vertical_lines: Border line between columns, for example `{ color: "#e5e7eb", width: 1 }`.
properties.data_row_min_height: Minimum height of a data row, in logical pixels.
properties.data_row_max_height: Maximum height of a data row, in logical pixels.
properties.heading_row_height: Height of the heading row, in logical pixels.
properties.viewport_fraction: Share of the viewport each page fills; below 1.0 the neighbouring pages show at the edges.
properties.pad_ends: Adds space before the first and after the last page when `viewport_fraction` is below 1.0.
properties.snap: Snaps to a resting position, such as a whole page, when the user stops dragging.
properties.keep_page: Restores the current page when the page view is rebuilt.
properties.implicit_scrolling: Lets assistive technology move to the next and previous page.
properties.force_actions_below: Puts the actions under the message instead of beside it.
properties.notch_margin: Space between the floating action button and the notch, in logical pixels.
properties.full_screen: Opens the search view full screen.
properties.shrink_wrap: Sizes the control to its content instead of filling the available space.
properties.bar_elevation: Shadow depth of the search bar.
properties.bar_leading: Control shown at the start of the search bar.
properties.bar_trailing: Controls shown at the end of the search bar.
properties.bar_size_constraints: Size limits of the search bar.
properties.view_elevation: Shadow depth of the search view.
properties.view_leading: Control shown at the start of the search view's header.
properties.view_trailing: Controls shown at the end of the search view's header.
properties.view_size_constraints: Size limits of the search view.
properties.year_2023: Uses the 2023 Material 3 design; set `false` for the newer look.
properties.track_gap: Gap between the active and inactive parts of the track, in logical pixels.
properties.affinity: Where the expand icon sits: `"leading"`, `"trailing"` or `"platform"`.
properties.collapsed_shape: Shape of the tile while collapsed.
properties.unit_id: Your AdMob ad unit ID; without it the client loads Google's test ad unit.
properties.request: Targeting options for the ad request, such as keywords.
properties.active_thumb_image_src: Image drawn on the thumb while the switch is on.
properties.inactive_thumb_image_src: Image drawn on the thumb while the switch is off.
properties.item_count: Number of items in the indicator, for variants that draw several.
properties.wave_type: Where the wave starts for wave variants: `"start"`, `"center"` or `"end"`.
properties.horizontal_grid_lines: Horizontal grid lines across the chart, for example `{ interval: 10, color: "#e5e7eb", width: 1 }`.
properties.vertical_grid_lines: Vertical grid lines across the chart, for example `{ interval: 1, color: "#e5e7eb", width: 1 }`.
properties.baseline_x: x value the chart draws from.
properties.baseline_y: y value the chart draws from, such as the bottom of the bars.
properties.coordinates: Position on the map as `[latitude, longitude]` or `{ latitude:, longitude: }`; a list of positions for lines and shapes.
properties.refresh_displacement: Distance, in logical pixels, the pull-to-refresh indicator settles at while refreshing (default 40).
properties.refresh_trigger_distance: How far, in logical pixels, the user must pull on iOS to start a refresh.
properties.refresh_timeout: Longest time, in milliseconds, the refresh indicator waits for `on_refresh` (default 30 seconds).
properties.enable_alpha: Lets the user pick a transparency value as well as a color.
properties.prefix_icon_size_constraints: Size limits for the prefix icon.
properties.suffix_icon_size_constraints: Size limits for the suffix icon.
properties.show_drag_handle: Shows a drag handle at the top of the sheet.
properties.automatically_imply_leading: Adds a back or menu button automatically when the page has somewhere to go back to or a drawer.
properties.transition_between_routes: Animates the bar between pages on iOS.
properties.previous_page_title: Title of the previous page, shown next to the iOS back button.
properties.animate: Animates the container's size, padding, colors, border and other decoration when they change: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `animation(300, curve: "easeOut")`.
properties.center_title: Centers the title in the bar; Android, web, Windows and Linux only. iOS and macOS always center it.
properties.code_theme: Syntax highlighting theme for code blocks: a theme name such as `"atom-one-dark"`, `"github"` or `"monokai-sublime"`, or a hash of token styles.
properties.error_content: Control shown in place of the image when it fails to load.
properties.foreground_decoration: Decoration painted over the content: `{ bgcolor:, gradient:, border:, border_radius:, shadows:, image:, shape:, blend_mode: }`.
properties.image: Background image painted behind the content: `{ src:, fit:, alignment:, repeat:, opacity: }`.
properties.shadow: Drop shadow, or a list of them: `{ color:, offset: { x:, y: }, blur_radius:, spread_radius: }`.
properties.src_base64: The image as a Base64 string, used when `src` is not set. `src` also accepts a Base64 string, which works with every release.

events.on_click: Fired when the control is clicked/tapped.
events.on_change_start: Fired when the user starts changing the value.
events.on_change_end: Fired when the user finishes changing the value.
events.on_submit: Fired when the input is submitted.
events.on_focus: Fired when the control gains focus.
events.on_blur: Fired when the control loses focus.
events.on_hover: Fired when the pointer enters/leaves the control.
events.on_tap_down: Fired when a pointer presses down; `event.local_position` and `event.global_position` give the point and `event.kind` the device, such as `"touch"` or `"mouse"`.
events.on_tap_cancel: Fired when a tap is cancelled.
events.on_tap_outside: Fired when a tap occurs outside the control.
events.on_dismiss: Fired when the control is dismissed.
events.on_scroll: Fired as the content scrolls, at most once per `scroll_interval`. `event.data` has `"event_type"` (`"start"`, `"update"`, `"end"`, `"user"` or `"overscroll"`), `"pixels"`, `"min_scroll_extent"`, `"max_scroll_extent"` and `"viewport_dimension"`, plus `"scroll_delta"` on updates, `"direction"` on user events, and `"overscroll"` and `"velocity"` on overscroll.
events.on_select: Fired when a selection is made.
events.on_selection_change: Fired when the user changes the selected text; `event.data` describes the new selection.
events.on_state_change: Fired when the control's state changes.
events.on_enter: Fired when the pointer enters the control.
events.on_exit: Fired when the pointer leaves the control.
events.on_image_error: Fired when an image the control shows fails to load; `event.data` describes the failure.
events.on_loaded: Fired when the control has loaded.
events.on_visible: Fired when the control becomes visible.
events.on_resize: Fired when the control is resized.
events.on_animation_end: Fired when an `animate_*` animation finishes. `event.data` names the animation: `"opacity"`, `"rotation"`, `"scale"`, `"offset"`, `"align"`, `"margin"` or `"position"`; a container's own `animate` reports `"container"`.
events.on_size_change: Fired after the control's size changes, at most once per `size_change_interval`. `event.data` is `{ "w" => width, "h" => height }` in logical pixels.
events.on_action_result: Fired when a client `action:` has finished; the event carries its result or error.
events.on_end_reached: Fired when the user scrolls within `end_reached_threshold` of the end, for loading more items. It fires once per content length: add items, and it can fire again. `event.data` has `"pixels"`, `"max_scroll_extent"` and `"viewport_dimension"`.
events.on_refresh: Fired when the user pulls down to refresh; the indicator spins until the handler returns.
events.on_paste_files: Fired when the user pastes files into the field; `event.files` lists them.
events.on_tap_outside_view: Fired when the user taps outside the open search view.
events.on_tap_outside_bar: Fired when the user taps outside the search bar.
events.on_reading: Fired with each new sensor reading in `event.data`.
events.on_event: Fired on chart or map touch and pointer events; `event.data` describes the event.
events.on_load: Fired when the content has loaded.
events.on_cancel: Fired when the menu closes without a choice.
events.on_impression: Fired when the ad is shown to the user.
events.on_will_dismiss: Fired just before a screen the ad opened closes.
events.on_paid: Fired when the ad earns revenue; `event.data` holds the value and currency.
events.on_reorder: Fired when an item is dropped in a new position; `event.old_index` and `event.new_index` give the move.
events.on_reorder_start: Fired when the user starts dragging an item.
events.on_reorder_end: Fired when the user drops a dragged item.
events.on_confirm_dismiss: Fired before the control is dismissed. Reply with `page.invoke(event.control, "confirm_dismiss", args: { dismiss: true })`, or `dismiss: false` to keep it; without a reply the client cancels the dismissal after five minutes.
events.on_update: Fired while the control is dragged, with the direction and progress.
events.on_select_all: Fired when the header checkbox selects or clears every row.
events.on_select_change: Fired when the row's checkbox is toggled.
events.on_sort: Fired when the column heading is tapped to sort; `event.data` has the column index (`ci`) and the new direction (`asc`).
events.on_tap_up: Fired when a pointer that pressed down lifts.
events.on_pan_start: Fired when a drag in any direction starts.
events.on_pan_update: Fired as a drag moves; `event.local_delta` is the movement since the last update.
events.on_pan_end: Fired when a drag ends; the event carries the velocity.
events.on_horizontal_drag_start: Fired when a horizontal drag starts.
events.on_horizontal_drag_update: Fired as a horizontal drag moves.
events.on_horizontal_drag_end: Fired when a horizontal drag ends.
events.on_vertical_drag_start: Fired when a vertical drag starts.
events.on_vertical_drag_update: Fired as a vertical drag moves.
events.on_vertical_drag_end: Fired when a vertical drag ends.
events.on_scale_start: Fired when a pinch or two-finger rotation starts.
events.on_scale_update: Fired as a pinch or rotation changes.
events.on_scale_end: Fired when a pinch or rotation ends.
events.on_entry_mode_change: Fired when the user switches between calendar and text input.
events.on_upload: Fired with the progress of a file upload.
events.on_color_change: Fired when the user picks a color; `event.data` is the color.
events.on_action: Fired when the action button is pressed.
events.on_secondary_tap_down: Fired when a secondary (right) button presses down; `event.local_position` and `event.global_position` give the point.

absorbpointer.absorbing: When true (default), the content gets no taps or other pointer input, and neither does anything behind it. Set `false` to let the content react again.
absorbpointer.content: The control whose pointer input is blocked; the first positional argument sets it.

animatedswitcher.content: The control shown now. Replace it with `page.update(switcher, content: ...)` to animate to the new one.
animatedswitcher.duration: Length of the animation to new content, in milliseconds (default 1000).
animatedswitcher.reverse_duration: Length of the animation of the outgoing content, in milliseconds (default: `duration`).
animatedswitcher.switch_in_curve: Easing curve of the incoming content, for example `"easeOut"` (default linear).
animatedswitcher.switch_out_curve: Easing curve of the outgoing content, for example `"easeIn"` (default linear).

autocomplete.on_select: Fired when a suggestion is picked; `event.value` is its value and `event.selection` holds its key and value.

badge.alignment: Corner the badge sits on, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1 (default the top right, `{ x: 1, y: -1 }`).
badge.bgcolor: Color of the badge (red by default).
badge.label: Text or control shown in the badge; the first positional argument sets it. Give a String: a number shows nothing, so write `badge(count.to_s)`. Without a label, Android, web, Windows and Linux draw a small dot; iOS and macOS need a label.
badge.label_visible: Shows the badge (default `true`); `false` hides it without removing it.
badge.large_size: Height of a badge with a label, in logical pixels (default 16 on Android, web, Windows and Linux, 18 on iOS and macOS).
badge.offset: Moves the badge from its corner, as `{ x:, y: }` in logical pixels.
badge.padding: Horizontal space between the label and the badge's edge, in logical pixels.
badge.small_size: Diameter of the dot drawn when the badge has no label, in logical pixels (default 6 on Android, web, Windows and Linux).
badge.text_color: Color of the label text (white by default).
badge.text_style: Text style of the label, as a hash such as `{ size: 10, weight: "bold" }`.

barchart.group_alignment: How the bar groups are spread along the x axis, for example `"spaceEvenly"` or `"center"`.

bottomsheet.dismissible: When false, tapping outside the sheet does not close it (default true).
bottomsheet.modal: On iOS and macOS, when true, tapping outside the sheet does not close it; `dismissible` wins when both are set. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it, so use `dismissible: false` to keep the sheet open everywhere.

button.default: Only an alert dialog's action on iOS and macOS uses it: the action shows in bold as the default one.
button.destructive: Only an alert dialog's action on iOS and macOS uses it: the action shows in red as destructive.
button.min_size: Minimum width and height of the button on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
button.opacity_on_click: Opacity, from 0.0 to 1.0, the button fades to while it is pressed on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
button.size: Size of the button on iOS and macOS: `"small"`, `"medium"` or `"large"` (the default). Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.

card.semantic_container: Treats the card and its content as one element for screen readers (default `true`); `false` lets screen readers visit each child on its own.
card.show_border_on_foreground: Draws the `shape` border over the content instead of behind it (default `true`). Android, web, Windows and Linux only; iOS and macOS ignore it.

carouselview.consume_max_weight: With `flex_weights`, lets items grow to the largest weight as they scroll in (default `true`); `false` keeps the layout fixed. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
carouselview.enable_splash: Shows the tap ripple or highlight on items (default `true`).
carouselview.horizontal: Scrolls the items horizontally (default `true`); `false` scrolls them vertically.
carouselview.flex_weights: A weighted layout such as `[1, 7, 1]`: the visible items share the width in these proportions. It wins over `item_extent`.
carouselview.initial_item: Index of the item shown first (default 0).
carouselview.item_clip_behavior: How each item is clipped to its rounded shape: `"antiAlias"` (default), `"hardEdge"`, `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"` or `"none"`.
carouselview.item_extent: Width of each item in logical pixels (height when `horizontal: false`). A carousel needs `item_extent` or `flex_weights`.
carouselview.item_snapping: Snaps to the nearest item when the user stops scrolling (default `false`).
carouselview.overlay_color: Color of the highlight drawn over an item while it is pressed or hovered.
carouselview.shrink_extent: Smallest size, in logical pixels, an item shrinks to as it scrolls off the edge (default 0). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
carouselview.on_item_click: Fired when the user taps an item; `event.data` is its index.

checkbox.error: Shows the checkbox in its error color. iOS and macOS ignore it.

circleavatar.max_radius: Largest radius the avatar may grow to, in logical pixels.
circleavatar.min_radius: Smallest radius the avatar may shrink to, in logical pixels.
circleavatar.radius: Radius of the avatar, in logical pixels (default 20).
circleavatar.on_image_error: Fired when `foreground_image_src` or `background_image_src` fails to load; `event.data` is `"foreground"` or `"background"`.

clipoval.clip_behavior: How the edge is clipped: `"antiAlias"` (default), `"hardEdge"`, `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"` or `"none"`.
clipoval.content: The control to clip; the first positional argument sets it.

cliprsuperellipse.border_radius: Corner radius: one number for every corner, or `{ top_left:, top_right:, bottom_left:, bottom_right: }` (missing corners stay square).
cliprsuperellipse.clip_behavior: How the edge is clipped: `"antiAlias"` (default), `"hardEdge"`, `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"` or `"none"`.
cliprsuperellipse.content: The control to clip; the first positional argument sets it.

column.animate_changes: Animates children that `page.update` adds or removes, as `item_animation` says (default `false`). It has no effect with `wrap: true`.
column.alignment: How the children are spread vertically: `"start"` (default), `"center"`, `"end"`, `"spaceBetween"`, `"spaceAround"` or `"spaceEvenly"`.
column.horizontal_alignment: How the children are aligned horizontally: `"start"` (default), `"center"`, `"end"` or `"stretch"`.
column.intrinsic_width: Makes the column as wide as its widest child.
column.item_animation: How `animate_changes` animates added and removed children: `{ type:, duration:, curve: }`, where `type` is `"fade"`, `"size"`, `"fade_size"` (default) or `"slide"` and `duration` defaults to 250 milliseconds.
column.refresh_bgcolor: Background color of the pull-to-refresh indicator. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
column.refresh_displacement: Distance, in logical pixels, the pull-to-refresh indicator settles at while refreshing (default 40). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
column.refresh_trigger_distance: How far, in logical pixels, the user must pull to start a refresh. iOS and macOS only.
column.run_alignment: With `wrap: true`, how the columns of children are spread horizontally: `"start"` (default), `"center"`, `"end"`, `"spaceBetween"`, `"spaceAround"` or `"spaceEvenly"`.
column.run_spacing: With `wrap: true`, space between the columns of children, in logical pixels (default 10).
column.spacing: Space between the children, in logical pixels (default 10).
column.wrap: Flows the children into a new column when they do not fit vertically, instead of overflowing.

container.alignment: Where the content sits inside the container, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1; `"center"` is also accepted.
container.blur: Blurs what is behind the container (frosted glass): a sigma such as `10`, `[x, y]`, or `{ sigma_x:, sigma_y: }`.
container.border_radius: Corner radius, in logical pixels: one number, or `{ top_left:, top_right:, bottom_left:, bottom_right: }`. It also clips the content.
container.color_filter: Tints the container and its content: `{ color:, blend_mode: }`, for example `{ color: "#80000000", blend_mode: "darken" }`.
container.dark_theme: Theme for the controls inside the container while the app is in dark mode, in the same form as `page.dark_theme`.
container.ignore_interactions: Makes the container and its content ignore taps and other pointer input.
container.ink: Shows touch feedback on a clickable container: an ink ripple on Android, web, Windows and Linux, and a fade to `opacity_on_click` on iOS and macOS.
container.ink_color: Color of the ink ripple when `ink: true`. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
container.opacity_on_click: Opacity, from 0.0 to 1.0, a clickable container with `ink: true` fades to while it is pressed (default 0.4). iOS and macOS only.
container.padding: Space between the container's edge and its content, in logical pixels: one number, or `{ left:, top:, right:, bottom: }`.
container.theme: Theme for the controls inside the container, in the same form as `page.theme`.
container.theme_mode: Forces the container's content into `"light"` or `"dark"` mode, or `"system"`.
container.url: URL opened when the container is tapped.
container.on_click: Fired when the container is tapped.
container.on_hover: Fired when the pointer enters or leaves the container; `event.data` is `true` on enter and `false` on leave.

cupertinoactivityindicator.animating: On iOS and macOS, spins the indeterminate indicator while true; set `false` to pause it. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
cupertinoactivityindicator.radius: Radius of the activity indicator on iOS and macOS, in logical pixels. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.

cupertinobottomsheet.dismissible: When false, tapping outside the sheet does not close it (default true).
cupertinobottomsheet.modal: On iOS and macOS, when true, tapping outside the sheet does not close it; `dismissible` wins when both are set. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it. To keep a sheet open on every platform, build it with `bottom_sheet(..., dismissible: false)`: both helpers send the same `BottomSheet` control.

cupertinodatepicker.inline: Draws the picker where you add it; this helper sends `true`. With `false` it is a dialog that `page.show_dialog` opens.

cupertinoslidingsegmentedbutton.bgcolor: Color of the track behind the segments, on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
cupertinoslidingsegmentedbutton.proportional_width: On iOS and macOS, sizes each segment to its content instead of giving all segments the same width. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
cupertinoslidingsegmentedbutton.thumb_color: Color of the thumb that slides to the selected segment, on iOS and macOS. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.

customscrollview.controls: The slivers, when they are given in a block; prefer `slivers`.
customscrollview.slivers: The slivers, in scroll order: `sliver_app_bar`, `sliver_list`, `sliver_grid`, `sliver_to_box_adapter`, `sliver_fill_remaining`, `sliver_padding`, or any other control, which scrolls as one box. The first positional argument sets them.

datacolumn.on_sort: Fired when the column heading is tapped to sort; `event.data` has the column index (`ci`) and `asc`, the new direction on Android, web, Windows and Linux. On iOS and macOS `asc` is the table's current `sort_ascending`, so keep the direction in Ruby.

datacolumn2.size: Relative width of the column: `"s"` (default), `"m"` or `"l"`.

dismissible.on_dismiss: Fired when the control has been swiped away; `event.direction` is the swipe direction, such as `"startToEnd"` or `"endToStart"`. Remove the control from its parent in this handler.
dismissible.on_resize: Fired while the space left by the dismissed control closes.
dismissible.on_update: Fired while the user drags; `event.direction` is the direction, `event.progress` how far the control has moved (0.0 to 1.0) and `event.reached` whether it is past the dismiss threshold.

divider.height: Total height the divider takes, with the line in the middle (default 16 on Android, web, Windows and Linux, 1 on iOS and macOS).
divider.leading_indent: Empty space before the line starts, in logical pixels (default 0).
divider.radius: Corner radius of the line's ends, in logical pixels.
divider.thickness: Thickness of the line, in logical pixels (default 0.5 on iOS and macOS).
divider.trailing_indent: Empty space after the line ends, in logical pixels (default 0).

draggable.affinity: Axis a drag must start along to pick the control up: `"horizontal"` or `"vertical"`.
draggable.axis: Restricts the drag to `"horizontal"` or `"vertical"` movement.
draggable.content: The control the user picks up; the first positional argument sets it.
draggable.content_feedback: Control shown under the pointer while dragging (default: the content at half opacity).
draggable.content_when_dragging: Control left in place of the content while it is being dragged (default: the content itself).
draggable.group: Name of the drag group (default `"default"`); only a `drag_target` with the same `group` accepts the drop.
draggable.max_simultaneous_drags: How many drags of this control may run at once; `0` turns dragging off.
draggable.on_drag_complete: Fired when the control was dropped on a target that accepted it; `event.data` is the group name.
draggable.on_drag_start: Fired when the user starts dragging the control.

draggablescrollablesheet.elevation: Shadow depth of the sheet. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
draggablescrollablesheet.extent_change_interval: Minimum time between two `on_extent_change` events, in milliseconds (default 50); a finished drag always reports where the sheet stopped.
draggablescrollablesheet.initial_child_size: Size of the sheet when it first shows, as a fraction of its parent's height (default 0.5).
draggablescrollablesheet.max_child_size: Largest size of the sheet, as a fraction of its parent's height (default 1.0).
draggablescrollablesheet.min_child_size: Smallest size of the sheet, as a fraction of its parent's height (default 0.25).
draggablescrollablesheet.should_close_on_min_extent: Lets dragging the sheet to its minimum size close an enclosing modal sheet (default `true`).
draggablescrollablesheet.snap_animation_duration: How long snapping to a size takes, in milliseconds.
draggablescrollablesheet.snap_sizes: Extra sizes, as fractions between `min_child_size` and `max_child_size`, that the sheet can snap to when `snap: true`.
draggablescrollablesheet.on_extent_change: Fired as the sheet size changes; `event.data` has `"extent"`, `"min"` and `"max"`, as fractions of the parent's height.

dragtarget.content: The control the user drops onto; the first positional argument sets it.
dragtarget.group: Name of the drag group this target accepts (default `"default"`). It accepts only a `draggable` with the same `group`.
dragtarget.on_accept: Fired when a draggable of the same group is dropped on the target; `event.src_id` is the draggable's id (look it up with `page.get_control(event.src_id)`) and `event.x` / `event.y` where it was dropped.
dragtarget.on_leave: Fired when a dragged control leaves the target without being dropped. The client sends the draggable's id as a two-item list, so read it from `event.data[1]`; `event.src_id` is nil here.
dragtarget.on_move: Fired as a dragged control of the same group moves over the target; `event.src_id` is its id and `event.x` / `event.y` its position.
dragtarget.on_will_accept: Fired when a dragged control enters the target; `event.accept` is true when its group matches, and `event.src_id` is its id.

dropdown.align_label_with_hint: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.alignment: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.collapsed: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.counter: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.counter_style: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.disabled_hint_content: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.enable_feedback: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.error: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.error_max_lines: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.fit_parent_size: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.focus_color: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.focused_bgcolor: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.focused_color: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.helper: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.helper_max_lines: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.hint_content: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.hint_fade_duration: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.hint_max_lines: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.icon: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.item_height: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.options_fill_horizontally: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.padding: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.prefix: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.prefix_icon_size_constraints: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.prefix_style: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.select_icon_disabled_color: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.select_icon_enabled_color: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.select_icon_size: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.size_constraints: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.suffix: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.suffix_icon: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.suffix_icon_size_constraints: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.suffix_style: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.text_vertical_align: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client uses it on a dropdown.
dropdown.on_click: Accepted so `dropdown_m2` code keeps loading; no Ruflet client fires it on a dropdown.
dropdown.on_change: The `dropdown_m2` spelling of `on_select`; the handler runs when an option is picked.

fadetransition.animating: Runs the animation while true (default); `false` pauses it where it is, and `true` resumes it.
fadetransition.curve: Easing curve of each run, for example `"easeInOut"` (default linear).
fadetransition.delay: Milliseconds to wait before the first run.
fadetransition.duration: Length of one run, in milliseconds (default 1000).
fadetransition.reverse: With `repeat: true`, plays back and forth instead of restarting from `begin`.
fadetransition.on_animation_end: Fired when a run that does not repeat finishes; `event.data` is `"transition"`. An `animate_*` animation on the same control reports its own name, as on other controls.
fadetransition.begin: Opacity the animation starts from, from 0 to 1 (default 0).
fadetransition.end: Opacity the animation ends at, from 0 to 1 (default 1).
fadetransition.content: The control to fade; the first positional argument sets it.

fittedbox.alignment: Where the scaled content sits in the box, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1 (default the center).
fittedbox.clip_behavior: How content that does not fit is clipped: `"none"` (default), `"hardEdge"`, `"antiAlias"` or `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"`.
fittedbox.content: The control to scale; the first positional argument sets it.
fittedbox.fit: How the content is scaled into the box: `"contain"` (default), `"cover"`, `"fill"`, `"fitWidth"`, `"fitHeight"`, `"scaleDown"` or `"none"`.

formrow.prefix: Label or control shown at the start of the row.
formrow.helper: Text or control shown below the row.
formrow.error: Error text or control shown below the row.

fractionallysizedbox.alignment: Where the sized content sits in the available space, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1 (default the center).
fractionallysizedbox.content: The control to size; the first positional argument sets it.
fractionallysizedbox.height_factor: Height as a fraction of the height the parent offers, such as `0.5`; leave it out to let the content choose. The parent must bound the height.
fractionallysizedbox.width_factor: Width as a fraction of the width the parent offers, such as `0.5`; leave it out to let the content choose. The parent must bound the width.

gesturedetector.on_double_tap_cancel: Fired when a possible double tap turns out not to be one.
gesturedetector.on_double_tap_down: Fired when the second tap of a double tap presses down; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_enter: Fired when a mouse pointer enters the control; `event.local_position`, `event.global_position` and `event.kind` describe it.
gesturedetector.on_exit: Fired when a mouse pointer leaves the control; `event.local_position` and `event.global_position` give where.
gesturedetector.on_force_press_end: Fired when a pressure-sensitive press ends; `event.pressure` is the last pressure. Only devices with force touch send it.
gesturedetector.on_force_press_peak: Fired when a pressure-sensitive press reaches its peak; `event.pressure` gives the pressure.
gesturedetector.on_force_press_start: Fired when a pressure-sensitive press starts; `event.pressure` gives the pressure.
gesturedetector.on_force_press_update: Fired as the pressure of a press changes; `event.pressure` and `event.local_position` describe it.
gesturedetector.on_horizontal_drag_cancel: Fired when a horizontal drag is cancelled before it starts.
gesturedetector.on_horizontal_drag_down: Fired when a pointer that may start a horizontal drag presses down; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_horizontal_drag_end: Fired when a horizontal drag ends; `event.velocity` is the speed in pixels per second and `event.primary_velocity` the horizontal part.
gesturedetector.on_horizontal_drag_start: Fired when a horizontal drag starts; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_horizontal_drag_update: Fired as a horizontal drag moves, at most once per `drag_interval`; `event.local_delta` is the movement since the last update and `event.primary_delta` its horizontal part.
gesturedetector.on_hover: Fired as a mouse pointer moves over the control, at most once per `hover_interval`; `event.local_position` gives the point and `event.local_delta` the movement.
gesturedetector.on_long_press_cancel: Fired when a press that could become a long press is cancelled.
gesturedetector.on_long_press_down: Fired when a pointer that may become a long press presses down; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_long_press_end: Fired when the finger lifts after a long press; `event.local_position` and `event.velocity` describe it.
gesturedetector.on_long_press_move_update: Fired as the finger moves during a long press; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_long_press_start: Fired when a long press is recognized; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_long_press_up: Fired when the finger lifts after a long press.
gesturedetector.on_multi_long_press: Fired after `multi_tap_touches` fingers stay down for a second.
gesturedetector.on_multi_tap: Fired when several fingers touch at once; `event.correct_touches` is true when the count reached `multi_tap_touches`.
gesturedetector.on_pan_cancel: Fired when a drag is cancelled before it starts.
gesturedetector.on_pan_down: Fired when a pointer that may start a drag presses down; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_pan_end: Fired when a drag in any direction ends; `event.velocity` is the speed in pixels per second.
gesturedetector.on_pan_start: Fired when a drag in any direction starts; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_pan_update: Fired as a drag moves, at most once per `drag_interval`; `event.local_delta` is the movement since the last update and `event.local_position` the point.
gesturedetector.on_right_pan_end: Fired when a drag with the right mouse button ends; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_right_pan_start: Fired when a drag with the right mouse button starts; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_right_pan_update: Fired as a right-button drag moves, at most once per `drag_interval`; `event.local_delta` is the movement since the last update.
gesturedetector.on_scale_end: Fired when a pinch or rotation ends; `event.velocity` and `event.pointer_count` describe it.
gesturedetector.on_scale_start: Fired when a pinch or two-finger rotation starts; `event.local_focal_point` and `event.pointer_count` describe it.
gesturedetector.on_scale_update: Fired as a pinch or rotation changes; `event.scale` is the scale since the start, `event.rotation` the rotation in radians and `event.focal_point_delta` the movement.
gesturedetector.on_scroll: Fired when the user scrolls with a mouse wheel or trackpad over the control; `event.scroll_delta` is the scroll amount and `event.local_position` the pointer.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_long_press: Fired on a long press with the secondary (right) button.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_long_press_cancel: Fired when a secondary-button press that could become a long press is cancelled.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_long_press_down: Fired when the secondary button presses down for a possible long press; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_long_press_end: Fired when the secondary button lifts after a long press; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_long_press_move_update: Fired as the pointer moves during a secondary-button long press.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_long_press_start: Fired when a secondary-button long press is recognized; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_long_press_up: Fired when the secondary button lifts after a long press.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_tap: Fired on a secondary (right-button) click; it carries no position, so use `on_secondary_tap_down` or `on_secondary_tap_up` for the point.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_tap_cancel: Fired when a secondary-button tap is cancelled.
gesturedetector.on_secondary_tap_up: Fired when a secondary button lifts after a tap; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_tap: Fired on a tap; `event.local_position` and `event.global_position` give the point where it pressed down.
gesturedetector.on_tap_cancel: Fired when a tap is cancelled, for example because the pointer moved away.
gesturedetector.on_tap_move: Fired as the pointer moves while pressed down; `event.delta` is the movement.
gesturedetector.on_tap_up: Fired when the pointer of a tap lifts; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_long_press: Fired on a long press with the middle mouse button.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_long_press_cancel: Fired when a middle-button press that could become a long press is cancelled.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_long_press_down: Fired when the middle button presses down for a possible long press; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_long_press_end: Fired when the middle button lifts after a long press.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_long_press_move_update: Fired as the pointer moves during a middle-button long press.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_long_press_start: Fired when a middle-button long press is recognized.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_long_press_up: Fired when the middle button lifts after a long press.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_tap_cancel: Fired when a middle-button tap is cancelled.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_tap_down: Fired when the middle mouse button presses down; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_tertiary_tap_up: Fired when the middle mouse button lifts; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_vertical_drag_cancel: Fired when a vertical drag is cancelled before it starts.
gesturedetector.on_vertical_drag_down: Fired when a pointer that may start a vertical drag presses down; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_vertical_drag_end: Fired when a vertical drag ends; `event.velocity` is the speed in pixels per second and `event.primary_velocity` the vertical part.
gesturedetector.on_vertical_drag_start: Fired when a vertical drag starts; `event.local_position` gives the point.
gesturedetector.on_vertical_drag_update: Fired as a vertical drag moves, at most once per `drag_interval`; `event.local_delta` is the movement since the last update and `event.primary_delta` its vertical part.

gridview.child_aspect_ratio: Width-to-height ratio of each cell (default 1, square cells).
gridview.max_extent: Largest width of a cell, in logical pixels (height for a horizontal grid); the grid fits as many columns as it can. It wins over `runs_count`.
gridview.refresh_bgcolor: Background color of the pull-to-refresh indicator. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
gridview.refresh_displacement: Distance, in logical pixels, the pull-to-refresh indicator settles at while refreshing (default 40). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
gridview.refresh_trigger_distance: How far, in logical pixels, the user must pull to start a refresh. iOS and macOS only.
gridview.run_spacing: Space between the columns of cells, in logical pixels (default 10).
gridview.runs_count: Number of columns (rows for a horizontal grid), default 1.
gridview.spacing: Space between the rows of cells, in logical pixels (default 10).

hero.content: The control that flies to its new place; the first positional argument sets it.
hero.tag: A value, such as a String, that pairs this hero with the hero of the same tag on the next view. Every hero on one view needs its own tag.
hero.transition_on_user_gestures: Also flies the hero when the user goes back with a gesture, such as the iOS back swipe (default `false`).

icon.apply_text_scaling: Scales the icon with the user's text size setting.
icon.fill: Fill of a variable icon font such as Material Symbols, from 0 (outlined) to 1 (filled). Fonts without that axis ignore it, like `grade`, `weight` and `optical_size`.
icon.grade: Grade (stroke thickness at the same size) of a variable icon font, for example -25 to 200.
icon.icon: Icon to show: a Material icon name such as `"settings"`, or `Ruflet::Icons` and `Ruflet::CupertinoIcons` constants; the first positional argument sets it.
icon.optical_size: Optical size of a variable icon font, for example 20 to 48.
icon.size: Size of the icon, in logical pixels (default 24).
icon.weight: Stroke weight of a variable icon font, for example 100 to 700.

ignorepointer.content: The control that ignores pointer input; the first positional argument sets it.
ignorepointer.ignoring: When true (default), the content ignores taps and other pointer input, which reach whatever lies behind it. Set `false` to let the content react again.

image.anti_alias: Smooths the image's edges when it is drawn scaled or rotated (default `false`).
image.cache_height: Decodes the image at this height, in physical pixels, to save memory for large images.
image.cache_width: Decodes the image at this width, in physical pixels, to save memory for large images.
image.color: Color blended into the image with `color_blend_mode`, for example to tint an icon-like image.
image.color_blend_mode: How `color` is blended into the image, for example `"srcIn"` to tint it or `"multiply"`.
image.fade_in_animation: Fades the image in once it has loaded: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `animation(300, curve: "easeOut")`.
image.fit: How the image fills its box: `"contain"`, `"cover"`, `"fill"`, `"fitWidth"`, `"fitHeight"`, `"scaleDown"` or `"none"`.
image.gapless_playback: Keeps showing the old image while a new `src` loads, instead of a blank space.
image.paint: How the image is drawn when it is a shape inside a `canvas`, built with `paint(...)`. An image on the page ignores it.
image.placeholder_fade_out_animation: Fades the placeholder out once the image has loaded: `true` (1000 ms, linear), a duration in milliseconds, or `animation(300, curve: "easeOut")`.
image.placeholder_fit: How the placeholder fills the box (default: `fit`).
image.placeholder_src: Image shown while `src` loads: a URL, an asset path or Base64 data.
image.repeat: Tiles the image to fill its box: `"noRepeat"` (default), `"repeat"`, `"repeatX"` or `"repeatY"`.
image.src: The image: a URL, a path in the app's assets, Base64 data or bytes; the first positional argument sets it.
image.x: Left edge of the image, in logical pixels, when it is a shape inside a `canvas`. An image on the page ignores it.
image.y: Top edge of the image, in logical pixels, when it is a shape inside a `canvas`. An image on the page ignores it.

indexedstack.alignment: Where a child smaller than the stack sits, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1 (default the top left).
indexedstack.fit: How the shown child is sized: `"loose"` (default, its own size), `"expand"` (the stack's size) or `"passThrough"`.
indexedstack.index: Index of the one child shown, starting at 0 (default 0). Every child stays built, so each keeps its state while hidden.

interactiveviewer.alignment: Accepted, but current clients cannot apply it: a viewer with `alignment` set fails to build. Leave it out.
interactiveviewer.boundary_margin: How far, in logical pixels, the content may be panned past the viewer's edges: one number or `{ left:, top:, right:, bottom: }` (default 0).
interactiveviewer.clip_behavior: How the content is clipped to the viewer: `"hardEdge"` (default), `"antiAlias"`, `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"` or `"none"`.
interactiveviewer.constrained: Lays the content out at the viewer's size (default `true`); `false` lets large content keep its own size, for panning around a big image or map.
interactiveviewer.interaction_end_friction_coefficient: How quickly a fling slows down after the user lets go (default 0.0000135); a larger value stops it sooner.
interactiveviewer.interaction_update_interval: Minimum time between two `on_interaction_update` events, in milliseconds (default 200).
interactiveviewer.pan_enabled: Lets the user pan the content with a drag (default `true`).
interactiveviewer.scale_enabled: Lets the user zoom with a pinch or the mouse wheel (default `true`).
interactiveviewer.scale_factor: How much one mouse wheel step zooms (default 200); a smaller value zooms faster.
interactiveviewer.on_interaction_end: Fired when the user lets go; `event.data` has `"pc"` (the pointer count) and `"v"`, the velocity as `{ "x", "y" }` in pixels per second.
interactiveviewer.on_interaction_start: Fired when the user starts to pan or zoom; `event.data` has `"lfp"` and `"gfp"` (the local and global focal point as `{ "x", "y" }`) and `"pc"` (the pointer count).
interactiveviewer.on_interaction_update: Fired as the user pans or zooms, at most once per `interaction_update_interval`; `event.data` has `"s"` (the scale since the start), `"rot"`, `"fpd"` (the focal point movement), `"lfp"`, `"gfp"` and `"pc"`.

intrinsicheight.content: The control to size to its own intrinsic height; the first positional argument sets it.

intrinsicwidth.content: The control to size to its own intrinsic width; the first positional argument sets it.
intrinsicwidth.step_height: Rounds the height up to a multiple of this value, in logical pixels.
intrinsicwidth.step_width: Rounds the width up to a multiple of this value, in logical pixels.

keyboardlistener.autofocus: Takes keyboard focus when the listener first shows. Without focus it receives no keys.
keyboardlistener.content: The control inside the listener; the first positional argument sets it.
keyboardlistener.include_semantics: Tells screen readers that the listener can take focus (default `true`).
keyboardlistener.on_key_down: Fired when a key is pressed; `event.data["key"]` is its label, such as `"A"`, `"Enter"` or `"Arrow Up"`.
keyboardlistener.on_key_repeat: Fired while a held key repeats; `event.data["key"]` is its label.
keyboardlistener.on_key_up: Fired when a key is released; `event.data["key"]` is its label.

listtile.dense: Uses a more compact layout with less vertical space. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.hover_color: Color of the tile while the pointer is over it. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.is_three_line: Gives the subtitle room for two lines, so the tile is three lines tall. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.shape: Shape of the tile's background and tap highlight. iOS and macOS ignore it.

listview.animate_changes: Animates items that `page.update` adds or removes, as `item_animation` says (default `false`).
listview.item_animation: How `animate_changes` animates added and removed items: `{ type:, duration:, curve: }`, where `type` is `"fade"`, `"size"`, `"fade_size"` (default) or `"slide"` and `duration` defaults to 250 milliseconds.
listview.refresh_bgcolor: Background color of the pull-to-refresh indicator. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
listview.refresh_displacement: Distance, in logical pixels, the pull-to-refresh indicator settles at while refreshing (default 40). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
listview.refresh_trigger_distance: How far, in logical pixels, the user must pull to start a refresh. iOS and macOS only.
listview.spacing: Space between items, in logical pixels (default 0).

markdown.auto_follow_links: Opens tapped links in the browser (default `false`); `on_tap_link` fires either way.
markdown.auto_follow_links_target: Where `auto_follow_links` opens a link on the web, for example `"_blank"` for a new tab.
markdown.code_style_sheet: Text styles for code blocks, in the same form as `md_style_sheet`.
markdown.extension_set: Markdown syntax extensions: `"none"` (default), `"commonMark"`, `"gitHubWeb"` or `"gitHubFlavored"`, which adds tables, task lists and strikethrough.
markdown.fit_content: Makes the markdown only as wide as its longest line (default `true`).
markdown.image_error_content: Control shown in place of an image in the markdown that fails to load.
markdown.latex_scale_factor: Scale of LaTeX formulas written as `$...$` or `$$...$$`.
markdown.md_style_sheet: Text styles per element, as a hash such as `{ h1_text_style: { size: 28 }, p_text_style: { size: 16 }, a_text_style: { color: "#2563eb" } }`.
markdown.selectable: Lets the user select the text and sends `on_selection_change` (default `false`).
markdown.shrink_wrap: Sizes the markdown to its content instead of filling the available height (default `true`).
markdown.soft_line_break: Keeps single line breaks in the source as line breaks instead of joining the lines (default `false`).
markdown.value: The Markdown source to render; the first positional argument sets it.
markdown.on_selection_change: Fired when the user changes the selection of a `selectable` markdown; `event.data["text"]` is the selected text.
markdown.on_tap_link: Fired when the user taps a link; `event.data` is the link's URL.
markdown.on_tap_text: Fired when the user taps text that is not a link.

mergesemantics.content: The control whose parts screen readers announce as one element; the first positional argument sets it.

navigationrail.group_alignment: Vertical position of the destinations, from -1.0 (top) to 1.0 (bottom).

nestedscrollview.body: The scrolling content under the headers, usually a `list_view`, `grid_view`, `custom_scroll_view` or `tabs` view.
nestedscrollview.controls: The header slivers, when they are given in a block; prefer `header_slivers`.
nestedscrollview.float_header_slivers: Shows a floating header again as soon as the user scrolls back up, before the body reaches its top (default `false`).
nestedscrollview.header_slivers: Slivers shown above the body that collapse as it scrolls, usually one `sliver_app_bar`; the first positional argument sets them.

overlay.controls: The controls drawn above the page; the first positional argument sets them.

pageview.selected_index: Index of the page shown, starting at 0. Setting it with `page.update` jumps to that page.
pageview.on_change: Fired when the user settles on another page; `event.data` is its index.

placeholder.color: Color of the box outline and its crossing lines (default a dark blue-grey).
placeholder.content: Optional control drawn inside the placeholder box.
placeholder.fallback_height: Height of the placeholder when its parent leaves the height open, in logical pixels (default 400).
placeholder.fallback_width: Width of the placeholder when its parent leaves the width open, in logical pixels (default 400).
placeholder.stroke_width: Width of the lines, in logical pixels (default 2).

popupmenubutton.on_select: Fired when an item is chosen; the data is the item's internal id, so handle each item's `on_click` instead.

progressring.animating: On iOS and macOS, spins the indeterminate indicator while true; set `false` to pause it. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
progressring.radius: Radius of the activity indicator on iOS and macOS, in logical pixels. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
progressring.stroke_cap: Shape of the ring's line ends: `"butt"`, `"round"` or `"square"`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.track_gap: Gap between the active and inactive parts of the ring's track, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.year_2023: On Android, web, Windows and Linux, uses the 2023 Material 3 design; set `false` for the newer look.

reorderabledraghandle.content: The control the user drags to move the list item, often an icon; the first positional argument sets it.
reorderabledraghandle.mouse_cursor: Cursor shown over the handle, for example `"grab"`.

reorderablelistview.spacing: Space between items, in logical pixels.
reorderablelistview.mouse_cursor: Cursor shown over the default drag handles. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
reorderablelistview.semantic_child_count: Accepted, but no Ruflet client reads it on a reorderable list.
reorderablelistview.on_reorder_end: Fired when the user drops the item, also when it lands where it started; `event.new_index` is the drop position.
reorderablelistview.on_reorder_start: Fired when the user starts dragging an item; `event.old_index` is its index.

responsiverow.columns: Number of virtual columns the row is divided into (default 12); `col` spans count in these.
responsiverow.alignment: How the children of a line are spread horizontally: `"start"` (default), `"center"`, `"end"`, `"spaceBetween"`, `"spaceAround"` or `"spaceEvenly"`.
responsiverow.breakpoints: Breakpoint names and the page width, in logical pixels, from which each applies (default `{ "xs" => 0, "sm" => 576, "md" => 768, "lg" => 992, "xl" => 1200, "xxl" => 1400 }`). They are compared with the page width, not the row's.
responsiverow.vertical_alignment: How the children of a line are aligned vertically: `"start"` (default), `"center"`, `"end"` or `"stretch"`.

rotatedbox.content: The control to rotate; the first positional argument sets it.
rotatedbox.quarter_turns: Number of clockwise quarter turns, such as `1` for 90 degrees (default 0). Unlike `rotate`, the layout turns with the content, so a turned box takes its rotated size.

rotationtransition.animating: Runs the animation while true (default); `false` pauses it where it is, and `true` resumes it.
rotationtransition.curve: Easing curve of each run, for example `"easeInOut"` (default linear).
rotationtransition.delay: Milliseconds to wait before the first run.
rotationtransition.duration: Length of one run, in milliseconds (default 1000).
rotationtransition.reverse: With `repeat: true`, plays back and forth instead of restarting from `begin`.
rotationtransition.on_animation_end: Fired when a run that does not repeat finishes; `event.data` is `"transition"`. An `animate_*` animation on the same control reports its own name, as on other controls.
rotationtransition.alignment: Point the content turns around, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1 (default the center).
rotationtransition.begin: Rotation the animation starts from, in full turns (default 0).
rotationtransition.end: Rotation the animation ends at, in full turns (default 1, one full turn).
rotationtransition.content: The control to rotate; the first positional argument sets it.

row.alignment: How the children are spread horizontally: `"start"` (default), `"center"`, `"end"`, `"spaceBetween"`, `"spaceAround"` or `"spaceEvenly"`.
row.intrinsic_height: Makes the row as tall as its tallest child, so `vertical_alignment: "stretch"` gives every child that height.
row.run_alignment: With `wrap: true`, how the lines of children are spread vertically: `"start"` (default), `"center"`, `"end"`, `"spaceBetween"`, `"spaceAround"` or `"spaceEvenly"`.
row.run_spacing: With `wrap: true`, space between the lines of children, in logical pixels (default 10).
row.spacing: Space between the children, in logical pixels (default 10).
row.vertical_alignment: How the children are aligned vertically: `"start"`, `"center"` (default), `"end"`, `"stretch"` or `"baseline"`.
row.wrap: Flows the children onto a new line when they do not fit horizontally, instead of overflowing.

ruflet_app.app_error_message: Message shown when the embedded app fails.
ruflet_app.app_startup_screen_message: Message shown on the startup screen while the embedded app connects.
ruflet_app.args: Arguments for the in-browser connection used with `force_pyodide`; a normal server URL ignores them.
ruflet_app.force_pyodide: Connects through the in-browser (Pyodide) channel instead of `url`'s WebSocket; kept for Flet compatibility, and Ruflet servers do not need it.
ruflet_app.reconnect_interval_ms: Time between reconnection attempts after the connection drops, in milliseconds.
ruflet_app.reconnect_timeout_ms: How long to keep trying to reconnect, in milliseconds.
ruflet_app.show_app_startup_screen: Shows a startup screen while the embedded app connects.
ruflet_app.url: Address of the Ruflet server to embed, such as `"http://localhost:8550"`.
ruflet_app.on_error: Fired when the embedded app reports an error; `event.data` is the message.

safearea.avoid_intrusions_bottom: Keeps the content clear of the bottom system area, such as the home indicator (default `true`).
safearea.avoid_intrusions_left: Keeps the content clear of system areas on the left (default `true`).
safearea.avoid_intrusions_right: Keeps the content clear of system areas on the right (default `true`).
safearea.avoid_intrusions_top: Keeps the content clear of the status bar and notch (default `true`).
safearea.maintain_bottom_view_padding: Keeps the bottom padding while the on-screen keyboard is open (default `false`).
safearea.minimum_padding: Least padding on each side even where the system needs none: one number or `{ left:, top:, right:, bottom: }`.

scaletransition.animating: Runs the animation while true (default); `false` pauses it where it is, and `true` resumes it.
scaletransition.curve: Easing curve of each run, for example `"easeInOut"` (default linear).
scaletransition.delay: Milliseconds to wait before the first run.
scaletransition.duration: Length of one run, in milliseconds (default 1000).
scaletransition.reverse: With `repeat: true`, plays back and forth instead of restarting from `begin`.
