scaletransition.on_animation_end: Fired when a run that does not repeat finishes; `event.data` is `"transition"`. An `animate_*` animation on the same control reports its own name, as on other controls.
scaletransition.alignment: Point the content scales around, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1 (default the center).
scaletransition.end: Scale the animation ends at (default 1, the normal size).
scaletransition.content: The control to scale; the first positional argument sets it.

screenshot.content: The control to capture; the first positional argument sets it.

searchbar.shrink_wrap: Sizes the search view to its suggestions.

selectionarea.content: The controls inside whose text the user can select together; the first positional argument sets it.
selectionarea.on_change: Fired when the selection changes; `event.data` is the selected text, or nil when nothing is selected.

semantics.header: Marks the content as a heading for screen readers.
semantics.expanded: Tells screen readers whether the content is expanded.
semantics.on_tap_hint_text: What screen readers say the tap action does, for example "Open".
semantics.on_long_press_hint_text: What screen readers say the long-press action does.
semantics.hint_text: What screen readers say acting on the control does, for example "Opens the message".
semantics.focus: Tells screen readers whether the control has input focus.
semantics.textfield: Tells screen readers that the content is a text field.
semantics.identifier: An identifier for UI tests and platform accessibility tools; screen readers do not announce it.
semantics.button: Tells screen readers the content is a button.
semantics.container: Makes the content its own element for screen readers instead of merging it into the parent (default `false`).
semantics.content: The control described to screen readers; the first positional argument sets it.
semantics.current_value_length: Number of characters entered so far, for a text field.
semantics.decreased_value: Value screen readers announce after `on_decrease`, such as `"40%"`.
semantics.exclude_semantics: Hides the content's own semantics, so screen readers announce only what this control says (default `false`).
semantics.focusable: Tells screen readers the content can take input focus.
semantics.heading_level: Heading level from 1 to 6, used with `header: true`.
semantics.hidden: Tells screen readers the content is hidden, such as an inactive page.
semantics.image: Tells screen readers the content is an image.
semantics.increased_value: Value screen readers announce after `on_increase`, such as `"60%"`.
semantics.label: Text screen readers announce for the content.
semantics.link: Tells screen readers the content is a link.
semantics.live_region: Announces changes to the label as they happen, as for a status message.
semantics.max_value_length: Largest number of characters allowed, for a text field.
semantics.mixed: Tells screen readers a checkbox is in a mixed (partly checked) state.
semantics.multiline: Tells screen readers a text field takes more than one line.
semantics.obscured: Tells screen readers a text field hides its text, as for a password.
semantics.read_only: Tells screen readers a text field cannot be edited.
semantics.selected: Tells screen readers the content is selected.
semantics.checked: Tells screen readers a checkbox or switch is checked.
semantics.slider: Tells screen readers the content is a slider.
semantics.toggled: Tells screen readers a switch is on.
semantics.value: Current value screen readers announce, such as `"50%"` for a slider. It does not change what is displayed.
semantics.on_copy: Fired when a screen reader asks to copy.
semantics.on_cut: Fired when a screen reader asks to cut.
semantics.on_decrease: Fired when a screen reader asks to decrease the value, for example with a swipe down on a slider.
semantics.on_did_gain_accessibility_focus: Fired when the screen reader's focus moves onto the content.
semantics.on_did_lose_accessibility_focus: Fired when the screen reader's focus leaves the content.
semantics.on_dismiss: Fired when a screen reader asks to dismiss the content.
semantics.on_increase: Fired when a screen reader asks to increase the value, for example with a swipe up on a slider.
semantics.on_move_cursor_backward_by_character: Fired when a screen reader moves the text cursor back one character; `event.data` is true when it extends the selection.
semantics.on_move_cursor_forward_by_character: Fired when a screen reader moves the text cursor forward one character; `event.data` is true when it extends the selection.
semantics.on_paste: Fired when a screen reader asks to paste.
semantics.on_scroll_down: Fired when a screen reader asks to scroll down.
semantics.on_scroll_left: Fired when a screen reader asks to scroll left.
semantics.on_scroll_right: Fired when a screen reader asks to scroll right.
semantics.on_scroll_up: Fired when a screen reader asks to scroll up.
semantics.on_set_text: Fired when a screen reader sets a text field's text; `event.data` is the new text.
semantics.on_tap: Fired when a screen reader activates the content, for example with a double tap in VoiceOver or TalkBack.
semantics.on_double_tap: Fired when the user double-taps the content.
semantics.on_long_press: Fired when a screen reader performs a long press on the content.

shadermask.blend_mode: How the shader is combined with the content (default `"modulate"`); `"srcIn"` paints the gradient only where the content is.
shadermask.border_radius: Clips the masked content to rounded corners, in logical pixels.
shadermask.content: The control to mask; the first positional argument sets it.
shadermask.shader: The gradient used as the mask: `{ _type: "linear", colors: [...], begin: { x:, y: }, end: { x:, y: } }`, with `_type` `"linear"`, `"radial"` or `"sweep"`. It is required.

shimmer.base_color: Color of the content between highlights. Give it with `highlight_color`, or use `gradient` instead.
shimmer.content: The placeholder controls the shimmer sweeps over, usually grey boxes; the first positional argument sets it.
shimmer.gradient: Gradient swept over the content instead of `base_color` and `highlight_color`: `{ _type: "linear", colors: [...] }`.
shimmer.loop: Number of sweeps before the shimmer stops; `0` (default) loops forever.
shimmer.period: Time one sweep takes, in milliseconds (default 1500).

sizetransition.animating: Runs the animation while true (default); `false` pauses it where it is, and `true` resumes it.
sizetransition.curve: Easing curve of each run, for example `"easeInOut"` (default linear).
sizetransition.delay: Milliseconds to wait before the first run.
sizetransition.duration: Length of one run, in milliseconds (default 1000).
sizetransition.reverse: With `repeat: true`, plays back and forth instead of restarting from `begin`.
sizetransition.on_animation_end: Fired when a run that does not repeat finishes; `event.data` is `"transition"`. An `animate_*` animation on the same control reports its own name, as on other controls.
sizetransition.axis: Direction the content grows in: `"vertical"` (default) or `"horizontal"`.
sizetransition.axis_alignment: Where the content is anchored along `axis` while it grows, from -1 (start) to 1 (end), default 0 (the middle).
sizetransition.begin: Size factor the animation starts from, as a fraction of the content's size along `axis` (default 0).
sizetransition.end: Size factor the animation ends at (default 1, the full size).
sizetransition.content: The control to grow; the first positional argument sets it.

slidetransition.animating: Runs the animation while true (default); `false` pauses it where it is, and `true` resumes it.
slidetransition.curve: Easing curve of each run, for example `"easeInOut"` (default linear).
slidetransition.delay: Milliseconds to wait before the first run.
slidetransition.duration: Length of one run, in milliseconds (default 1000).
slidetransition.reverse: With `repeat: true`, plays back and forth instead of restarting from `begin`.
slidetransition.on_animation_end: Fired when a run that does not repeat finishes; `event.data` is `"transition"`. An `animate_*` animation on the same control reports its own name, as on other controls.
slidetransition.begin: Position the animation starts from, as `{ x:, y: }` in fractions of the content's own size (default `{ x: 0, y: 1 }`, one height below).
slidetransition.end: Position the animation ends at (default `{ x: 0, y: 0 }`, its place in the layout).
slidetransition.content: The control to slide; the first positional argument sets it.

sliverappbar.always_show_middle: Shows the small title in the collapsed bar even while the large title is visible (default `true`). iOS and macOS only.
sliverappbar.bottom_height: Height of `bottom`, in logical pixels (default 48). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
sliverappbar.center_title: Centers the title in the bar. Android, web, Windows and Linux only; iOS and macOS always center it.
sliverappbar.collapsed_height: Height of the bar when fully collapsed, in logical pixels. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
sliverappbar.color: Color of the title and icons. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
sliverappbar.elevation: Shadow depth of the bar. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
sliverappbar.expanded_height: Height of the bar when fully expanded, in logical pixels. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
sliverappbar.flexible_space: Control shown behind the expanded bar on Android, web, Windows and Linux, such as a cover image; iOS and macOS show it below the bar.
sliverappbar.floating: Shows the bar again as soon as the user scrolls up (default `false`).
sliverappbar.pinned: Keeps the collapsed bar at the top while the content scrolls (default `true` for `"medium"` and `"large"`, `false` for `"small"`).
sliverappbar.scrolled_under_elevation: Shadow depth once content scrolls under the bar. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
sliverappbar.shadow_color: Color of the bar's shadow. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
sliverappbar.stretch: Stretches the bar when the user overscrolls at the top (default `false`).
sliverappbar.toolbar_height: Height of the toolbar row, in logical pixels. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.

sliverfillremaining.content: The control that fills the rest of the viewport; the first positional argument sets it.
sliverfillremaining.fill_overscroll: Stretches the content into the overscroll area instead of leaving it empty (default `false`).
sliverfillremaining.has_scroll_body: Set `true` when the content scrolls itself, such as a `list_view` (default `false`, a plain box that is at least as tall as the space left).

slivergrid.bgcolor: Background color behind the grid and its header.
slivergrid.child_aspect_ratio: Width-to-height ratio of each cell (default 1, square cells).
slivergrid.controls: The cells; the first positional argument sets them.
slivergrid.max_extent: Largest width of a cell, in logical pixels; the grid fits as many columns as it can. It wins over `runs_count`.
slivergrid.padding: Space around the grid, in logical pixels: one number or `{ left:, top:, right:, bottom: }`.
slivergrid.run_spacing: Space between the columns of cells, in logical pixels (default 10).
slivergrid.spacing: Space between the rows of cells, in logical pixels (default 10).
slivergrid.sticky_header: Keeps the `header` at the top while the cells scroll under it, until the grid scrolls away (default `false`).

sliverlist.bgcolor: Background color behind the list and its header.
sliverlist.controls: The items; the first positional argument sets them.
sliverlist.divider_thickness: Draws a divider of this thickness between items, in logical pixels, inside `spacing` (default 0, none).
sliverlist.item_extent: Height of every item, in logical pixels, which speeds up long lists.
sliverlist.padding: Space around the list, in logical pixels: one number or `{ left:, top:, right:, bottom: }`.
sliverlist.spacing: Space between items, in logical pixels (default 0).
sliverlist.sticky_header: Keeps the `header` at the top while the items scroll under it, until the list scrolls away (default `false`).

sliverpadding.controls: The slivers, when they are given in a block; prefer `slivers`.
sliverpadding.padding: Space around the slivers, in logical pixels: one number or `{ left:, top:, right:, bottom: }`.
sliverpadding.slivers: The slivers to inset, in order; a plain control among them scrolls as one box. The first positional argument sets them.

slivertoboxadapter.content: The control that scrolls as one box among the slivers; the first positional argument sets it.

snackbar.action: Label of the action button shown in the snack bar.
snackbar.duration: How long the snack bar stays visible, in milliseconds.

spinkit.variant: The indicator style; set it with the variant keyword you pass to `spinkit`, such as `three_bounce:`.
spinkit.size: Size of the indicator, in logical pixels (default 50).
spinkit.duration: Length of one animation cycle, in milliseconds.

stack.alignment: Where children without `left`, `top`, `right` or `bottom` sit, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1 (default the top left).
stack.clip_behavior: How children that reach outside the stack are clipped: `"hardEdge"` (default), `"antiAlias"`, `"antiAliasWithSaveLayer"` or `"none"`.
stack.fit: How children without a position are sized: `"loose"` (default, their own size), `"expand"` (the stack's size) or `"passThrough"`.

text.alignment: Where the text is anchored when it is a shape inside a `canvas`, as `{ x:, y: }`. Text on the page ignores it; use `text_align`.
text.ellipsis: Accepted, but only text drawn inside a `canvas` uses it. For text on the page, use `overflow: "ellipsis"` with `max_lines`.
text.enable_interactive_selection: With `selectable: true`, lets the user select (default `true`).
text.font_family: Font to use, such as a font you registered in `page.fonts` or a system font name.
text.font_family_fallback: Fonts to try, in order, for characters `font_family` lacks, such as `["Noto Sans Arabic"]`.
text.max_lines: Most lines the text takes; the rest is cut off, or ends with `overflow`.
text.max_width: Width at which the text wraps when it is a shape inside a `canvas`, in logical pixels. Text on the page ignores it.
text.no_wrap: Keeps the text on one line instead of wrapping it.
text.overflow: How text that does not fit ends: `"clip"`, `"fade"`, `"ellipsis"` (adds …) or `"visible"`. Combine it with `max_lines` or `no_wrap`.
text.selectable: Lets the user select and copy the text (default `false`).
text.selection_cursor_color: Color of the cursor and handles while the user selects.
text.selection_cursor_height: Height of the cursor while the user selects, in logical pixels. Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
text.selection_cursor_width: Width of the cursor while the user selects, in logical pixels (default 2). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
text.show_selection_cursor: Shows a blinking cursor in selectable text (default `false`). Android, web, Windows and Linux only.
text.spans: Inline pieces of text with their own style or link, built with `text_span(...)`, shown after `value`.
text.style: Text style as a hash, such as `{ size: 18, weight: "bold", color: "#111827" }`.
text.theme_style: One of the theme's text styles, such as `"headline_small"`, `"title_medium"` or `"body_small"`; `style` overrides its parts.
text.value: The text to show; the first positional argument sets it.
text.x: Horizontal position when the text is a shape inside a `canvas`, in logical pixels. Text on the page ignores it.
text.y: Vertical position when the text is a shape inside a `canvas`, in logical pixels. Text on the page ignores it.
text.on_selection_change: Fired when the user changes the selection of `selectable` text. `event.data` has `"selected_text"`, `"cause"` and `"selection"` with `"base_offset"` and `"extent_offset"`. On iOS and macOS `"selected_text"` is the selected part; on Android, web, Windows and Linux it is the whole text, so cut it with the offsets.
text.on_tap: Fired when the user taps the text. On Android, web, Windows and Linux it fires only for `selectable: true` text; iOS and macOS send it for any text.

textspan.semantics_label: Text screen readers announce instead of the span's text.
textspan.spans: Nested spans, which take this span's style as their default.
textspan.spell_out: Makes screen readers read the text letter by letter, for codes and abbreviations.
textspan.style: Text style of the span, such as `{ color: "#2563eb", decoration: "underline" }`.
textspan.text: The span's text; the first positional argument sets it.
textspan.url: URL opened when the user taps the span.
textspan.on_click: Fired when the user taps the span.
textspan.on_enter: Fired when a mouse pointer moves onto the span.
textspan.on_exit: Fired when a mouse pointer leaves the span.

transparentpointer.content: The control that receives pointer input while letting it through to the controls behind it; the first positional argument sets it.

verticaldivider.leading_indent: Empty space above the line, in logical pixels (default 0).
verticaldivider.radius: Corner radius of the line's ends, in logical pixels.
verticaldivider.thickness: Thickness of the line, in logical pixels (default 0.5 on iOS and macOS).
verticaldivider.trailing_indent: Empty space below the line, in logical pixels (default 0).
verticaldivider.width: Total width the divider takes, with the line in the middle (default 16 on Android, web, Windows and Linux, 1 on iOS and macOS).

windowdragarea.content: The control that works as the window's title bar; the first positional argument sets it.
windowdragarea.maximizable: Double-clicking the area maximizes or restores the window (default `true`).
windowdragarea.on_double_tap: Fired after a double click maximized or restored the window; `event.data` is `"maximize"` or `"unmaximize"`.
windowdragarea.on_drag_end: Fired when the user stops dragging the window; `event.velocity` gives the speed.
windowdragarea.on_drag_start: Fired when the user starts dragging the window; `event.local_position` gives the point.

carouselview.animate_to_item: Scrolls the mounted carousel so the item at `index` leads (default 300 ms, `"ease"`).

contextmenu.open: On iOS and macOS the menu cannot be opened from code; it opens only from the user's long press.

draggablescrollablesheet.animate_to: Animates the mounted sheet to `size`, a fraction of its parent's height (default 300 ms, `"easeOut"`).
draggablescrollablesheet.jump_to: Moves the mounted sheet to `size`, a fraction of its parent's height, at once.

interactiveviewer.pan: Moves the content by `dx` and `dy` logical pixels.
interactiveviewer.reset: Returns to no zoom and no pan; give `animation_duration:` in milliseconds to animate there.
interactiveviewer.restore_state: Returns to the zoom and pan kept by `save_state`.
interactiveviewer.save_state: Keeps the current zoom and pan for `restore_state`.
interactiveviewer.zoom: Multiplies the zoom by `factor`, within `min_scale` and `max_scale`: `zoom(1.5)` zooms in, `zoom(0.5)` out.

pageview.jump_to: Jumps to a scroll offset in logical pixels, which can stop between pages; use `jump_to_page` for a whole page.
pageview.jump_to_page: Shows the page at `index` at once.

screenshot.capture: Captures the content as a PNG and passes the bytes, as a binary String, to `on_result`. `pixel_ratio:` sets the resolution (pass a Float such as `2.0`) and `delay:` waits that many milliseconds first (default 20).
